Decompose a square matrix into symmetric and skew-symmetric parts

Source: R/proximity.R
asym_decomp.Rd

X = S + K with S = (X + t(X)) / 2 and K = (X - t(X)) / 2. The share of asymmetry is sum(K^2) / sum(X^2) (Gower, 1977). Missing values are ignored in the sums.

Usage

asym_decomp(x)

Arguments

x

A square proximity matrix (see as_proximity()).

Value

An object of class mdspace_asym with elements S, K, ss (sums of squares of X, S, K) and asymmetry.

References

Gower, J. C. (1977). The analysis of asymmetry and orthogonality. In J. R. Barra et al. (Eds.), Recent developments in statistics (pp. 109-123). North-Holland.

Examples

x <- matrix(c(0, 1, 1, 7, 1, 0, 1, 7, 7, 7, 0, 1, 1, 1, 7, 0), 4, byrow = TRUE)
asym_decomp(x)
#> Symmetric / skew-symmetric decomposition
#> Sum of squares: total = 252  symmetric = 162  skew = 90 
#> Share of asymmetry: 0.3571
